chunks: Al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from some of his freedmen who said:

I asked him about the nocturnal emission of the fasting person, so he said: 'If he emits semen during the day in the month of Ramadan, he is not allowed to sleep until he performs ghusl. And whoever becomes junub at night in the month of Ramadan, he should not sleep for an hour until he performs ghusl. So whoever becomes junub in the month of Ramadan and sleeps until morning, then upon him is freeing a slave or feeding sixty poor people and making up that day, and he completes it, and he will never catch up with it.'

key_terms.أَجْنَب: He became junub (in a state of major impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (kaffarah) for a fasting person in Ramadan who sleeps until morning in a state of major impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific rulings for a fasting person in Ramadan who experiences nocturnal emission (ihtilam), distinguishing between day and night emissions. It prescribes that one should not sleep until performing ritual bath (ghusl); if one sleeps until morning in a state of major impurity, they must pay a kaffarah (expiation) of freeing a slave or feeding sixty poor people, in addition to making up the fast for that day. The ruling emphasizes the importance of maintaining ritual purity during the holy month and the consequences of neglecting it.
